Things I built that other people use. All of them run in the browser or on a free host; source is on GitHub.

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [Step by Step SQL](https://zjschroeder.github.io/SQL_tutorial/)
A browser-only Shiny app that teaches SQL to people who already know data frames. Each tab builds one clause of a query on a live SQLite database (a fictional research institute with six linked tables and deliberately awkward NULLs), then hands you a live editor. Runs on webR, nothing to install. [Source](https://github.com/zjschroeder/SQL_tutorial)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [t-tests and ANOVA, step by step](https://zjschroeder.github.io/t_tests_and_anova/)
Five tests rebuilt from raw data for an undergraduate statistics lab, each step shown three ways at once: formal notation, plain English, and the lab's own scenario with real numbers. Okabe-Ito palette, automated tests in the repo, runs in the browser. [Source](https://github.com/zjschroeder/t_tests_and_anova)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [So, you want to be a teacher?](https://zjschroeder.github.io/teacher_salaries/)
An interactive dashboard on U.S. teacher salaries and working hours (R, flexdashboard, plotly). [Source](https://github.com/zjschroeder/teacher_salaries)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [LA28 Olympic schedule builder](https://zjschroeder.shinyapps.io/la28_scheduling_app/)
Rate every sport, set a ticket budget, and a greedy optimizer with zone-cohesion penalties builds a day-by-day schedule from 251 sessions, with charts and CSV/Excel export. First load takes a few seconds while the free host wakes up. [Source](https://github.com/zjschroeder/la28_scheduling_app)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### Empathic-accuracy data collection app
A Shiny app for collecting empathic-accuracy data online, used in the lab's studies. [Source](https://github.com/zjschroeder/Empathic-Accuracy-Data-Collection-App)
:::

:::
